_comment: Normals, not forecasts. Drives the growing calendar, the heating load and the season logic. Shape: schemas/locale.toml.
station_used: BREMERTON, WA US (NOAA GHCN ID USC00450872), 47.5689 N, -122.6828 W, elevation 33.5 m. 8.5 km (5.3 mi) due south of Silverdale center. This is the nearest station to Silverdale with a complete 1991-2020 temperature and freeze/frost Normals record; the ~15 closer stations are all CoCoRaHS precipitation-only sites with no temperature data. Winter design temperature only is from a second station, Bremerton National Airport (ICAO KPWT / WBAN USW00094263), 47.49 N, -122.76 W, elevation 135 m, 17.9 km (11.1 mi) SSW, because hourly design values require an airport station.
how_to_read_the_frost_dates: The average is the 50th percentile: in half of all years the last spring frost falls AFTER it. Planting tender crops to the average kills them in half of all years. Plant to late_90pct (April 24), the date past which only one year in ten still delivers a frost, and have row cover ready by early_10pct in autumn (October 26), not by the average. All thresholds are 32 F. At the 36 F threshold, which is the honest one for seedlings on a clear calm night, the 10-percent-risk spring date is May 13.
notes:
LICENSING: every value here is from a US federal source (NOAA NCEI, USDA ARS, US Naval Observatory) and is public domain. Nothing was taken from Wikipedia, iNaturalist, GBIF, OpenStreetMap or any CC BY-SA source.

HOW TO READ THE FROST DATES - THIS IS THE PART THAT COSTS CROPS. "average" is the 50th percentile: in half of all years the last spring frost falls AFTER March 29. Do not plant tender crops to it. "late_90pct" (April 24) is the date past which only 10 percent of years still deliver a frost; that is the plant-out date for tomatoes, beans, squash and basil. On the autumn side, "early_10pct" (October 26) is the date by which 10 percent of years have already had their first frost, so that is when row cover should be ready, not November 14.

I verified the percentile direction rather than assuming it, because reversing it is the single most damaging error possible here. Two independent confirmations: (1) NOAA's own variable documentation states "ANN-TMIN-PRBFST-T32FP10 provides the earliest date at which there is a 10% probability of a temperature of 32 or less"; (2) I recomputed last-spring and first-autumn freeze dates directly from the station's raw daily observations for 1991-2020 and took empirical percentiles. The raw data gives last spring frost p10/p50/p90 = Mar 16 / Mar 31 / Apr 23 and first autumn frost p10/p50/p90 = Nov 1 / Nov 16 / Dec 1, against the published Mar 5 / Mar 29 / Apr 24 and Oct 26 / Nov 14 / Dec 1. The median agrees within two days and the critical late-spring date within one day, which confirms the mapping. The published values are reported above since they are the authoritative product.

All frost values are at the 32 F (0 C) threshold. NOAA also publishes a 36 F threshold, which is the more honest number for frost-sensitive seedlings on a clear calm night: last spring 36 F at the 10-percent-risk level is May 13, and first autumn is October 4.

DATA COMPLETENESS, STATED PLAINLY: the Bremerton normals carry NOAA's "R" (Representative) completeness flag, not "S" (Standard). Counting raw observations, 20 of the 30 years in 1991-2020 have a near-complete daily record; 1991, 1997, 2002 and 2009 have substantial gaps that NOAA filled with estimates from surrounding stations. The normals are sound but are not a 30-year unbroken record.

HARDINESS ZONE: 8b (15 to 20 F / -9.4 to -6.7 C), read from USDA ARS's own ZIP-code table for 98383, the table that drives the official 2023 interactive map. Silverdale sits right on a zone boundary and this matters locally: ZIPs 98383 (Silverdale), 98312 (west Bremerton) and 98370 (Poulsbo) are 8b, while 98311 and 98337 nearer the Bremerton waterfront are 9a. Shoreline sites on Dyes Inlet run about half a zone warmer than sites a few hundred metres inland or uphill. As a cross-check I computed the mean annual extreme minimum temperature (which is what defines the zone) from raw 1991-2020 daily data at Bremerton: -6.7 C = 19.9 F, landing in 8b at the very top of its range, consistent with the official assignment and with how close the 9a line is.

KOPPEN: Csb, warm-summer Mediterranean. No federal agency publishes a Koppen letter for this point, so I computed it from the NOAA monthly normals above using the standard criteria, and the tests are not marginal: coldest month 4.6 C (so temperate C); driest summer month 21 mm, which is under the 40 mm threshold and is one twelfth of the 252 mm wettest winter month, far past the required one third (so summer-dry, s); warmest month 19.0 C with 7 months at or above 10 C (so warm-summer, b). This is the classification for the Puget Sound lowlands generally, driven by the very dry July and August visible in the table.

WINTER DESIGN TEMPERATURE: -6 C is the 99.6 percent annual occurrence dry-bulb from NOAA's Engineering Weather Data for Bremerton National Airport, period of record 1988-2017. The same table gives -3 C at 99 percent, -1 C at 97.5 percent, and a median annual extreme low of -9 C. I deliberately did NOT use the ASHRAE Handbook design tables, which are copyrighted and would contaminate the release licence; this NOAA publication is the public-domain equivalent. Note the caveat for a builder: this station is 11 miles away, inland, and 100 m higher than Silverdale, so it runs colder. Using it is conservative for a Silverdale site, but a permit application should carry whatever value the Kitsap County code official requires.

RECORD EXTREMES are from the full 1899-2026 daily record at Bremerton, quality-flagged values excluded. The high of 38.9 C (102 F) is 28 June 2021, the Pacific Northwest heat dome; the surrounding days read 37.8 and 38.3 C, so it is a real event, not a bad sensor. The low of -13.9 C (7 F) is 21 December 1990, inside a coherent five-day arctic outbreak (19-23 December read -7.8, -8.9, -13.9, -10.6, -10.0 C), again clearly real.

Annual precipitation 1446 mm (56.93 in) matches the sum of the twelve monthly normals exactly. The distribution is the thing to design around: December alone (252 mm) brings nearly as much rain as April through September put together (294 mm across those six months), which is about 86 percent of half a year in one month. Just under 80 percent of the year's water falls October through March (1,154 mm of the 1,448 mm the monthly table sums to), and there are about 102 days a year with 0.10 in or more of precipitation. A grower here needs summer irrigation despite the region's wet reputation; a builder needs winter drainage, not summer.

Daylight hours are sunrise-to-sunset for the 15th of each month at 47.6448 N, -122.6949 W, computed by the US Naval Observatory. I requested all twelve at a fixed UTC-8 offset with DST disabled so that daylight saving transitions cannot corrupt the interval arithmetic. Range is 8.4 h at midwinter to 16.0 h at midsummer.

sources.what: NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Monthly Climate Normals, station USC00450872 (Bremerton, WA): monthly mean maximum/minimum temperature and monthly precipitation normals

NOAA NCEI 1991-2020 Annual/Seasonal Climate Normals, station USC00450872: freeze/frost probability dates at the 32 F threshold (ANN-TMIN-PRBLST/PRBFST-T32FP10/50/90), growing season length (ANN-TMIN-PRBGSL-T32FP50 = 227 days), and annual precipitation normal (56.93 in)
NOAA NCEI Normals variable documentation: defines PRBFST, PRBLST and PRBGSL and states the percentile convention used to orient the 10/50/90 frost dates

NOAA NCEI Global Historical Climatology Network Daily, station USC00450872, raw daily observations 1899-2026: source for record high and record low, for the independent empirical recomputation of frost-date percentiles, and for the mean annual extreme minimum temperature used to cross-check the hardiness zone
NOAA NCEI GHCN-Daily station inventory: coordinates and elevation for USC00450872 and for all candidate stations screened within 45 km of Silverdale

USDA ARS 2023 Plant Hardiness Zone Map, official ZIP-code lookup table (the ArcGIS service owned by USDA ARS that powers the official map application): ZIP 98383 Silverdale returns 8b (15 to 20 F / -9.4 to -6.7 C)
USDA ARS 2023 Plant Hardiness Zone Map, public landing page for the above dataset

NOAA NCEI Engineering Weather Data, Bremerton National Airport (ICAO KPWT), SI units, period of record 1988-2017: winter design dry-bulb temperatures, 99.6 percent = -6 C, 99.0 percent = -3 C, 97.5 percent = -1 C, median of extreme lows = -9 C. Public-domain substitute for the copyrighted ASHRAE design tables

US Naval Observatory Astronomical Applications Department API: sunrise and sunset times at 47.6448 N, -122.6949 W for the 15th of each month, fixed UTC-8, DST disabled; source of the daylight_hours column (example request shown is June)
